data.name: MineFight
data.detailed_description:
MineFight is a 2D fighting game. Inspired by the universe of Minecraft. You control a character whose main weapon is a bow.
Playable with joystick and keyboard.

The gameplay is aggressive and fast, you need to combine shifting and aiming to overcome your enemies. You will soon learn how to use your bow and the physics of your arrows. To spice up all that special arrows are picked up as well as different sadistic traps.

The game features 12 characters inspired by 12 French Minecraft Youtubeurs. Owning each their skins and a special individual power to each.

The special powers will allow you to reverse the situation, but before you can activate it you will have to recover an orb on the map. Other experience orbs will serve you for arrows and traps. So move around more efficiently and quickly. But do not die.

Playable only in Local Multiplayer 2 with a keyboard and a controller!

reviews.review:
MineFight is a small-scale, free-to-play competitive action game that attempts to transform the familiar blocky aesthetic of Minecraft into a fast-paced, two-dimensional archery fighting experience. Developed and published by Talpel Games, the game emphasizes quick reflexes, precise aiming, strategic movement, and the ability to outsmart an opponent in unpredictable encounters. Its straightforward premise makes it relatively easy to understand, with two players battling across an arena using bows, special arrows, traps, and character-specific abilities. Although the concept has potential as a casual multiplayer distraction, its restrictive design and limited content prevent it from becoming a consistently satisfying competitive experience.

The combat system revolves around using a bow to eliminate an opponent while avoiding incoming projectiles. Unlike conventional fighting games built around melee combinations, MineFight requires players to understand arrow trajectories, anticipate enemy movement, and maintain favorable positioning. This creates an interesting balance between offensive aggression and defensive awareness. Every missed shot presents an opportunity for retaliation, while a well-timed attack can immediately change the momentum of an encounter. The physics-based projectile mechanics introduce a degree of skill, rewarding players who become familiar with aiming and movement. However, the relatively simple combat structure may eventually feel repetitive, particularly for those accustomed to fighting games with more elaborate mechanics and tactical possibilities.

One of its more engaging features is the inclusion of collectible experience orbs, special arrows, and environmental traps. These additions encourage players to move around the battlefield instead of remaining stationary and exchanging projectiles. Collecting certain orbs grants access to additional offensive tools, while another type enables a character's special ability. This creates moments of tactical decision-making, as players must determine whether pursuing valuable resources is worth exposing themselves to an opponent's attacks. Traps add another layer of danger, potentially punishing careless movement and creating opportunities for clever positioning. Although these mechanics introduce welcome variety, their effectiveness ultimately depends on how entertaining players find the underlying archery combat.

The game features twelve playable characters inspired by French Minecraft YouTubers, each possessing an individual appearance and unique special power. This character selection provides some variety and encourages experimentation with different abilities. Special powers can potentially reverse an unfavorable situation, giving players opportunities to recover from mistakes or surprise their opponents. The concept works particularly well for a lighthearted competitive experience, where unexpected reversals can be entertaining. Nevertheless, the roster's cultural references may not resonate with players unfamiliar with the personalities involved. Furthermore, character-specific abilities cannot entirely compensate for the relatively narrow range of activities available.

Visually, MineFight embraces a simple, colorful presentation heavily influenced by Minecraft's recognizable block-based style. Its uncomplicated graphics suit the game's modest ambitions and help maintain attention on the combat itself. The character designs contribute some personality, while the two-dimensional environments provide a straightforward setting for projectile exchanges. However, the artistic presentation lacks the originality and visual sophistication necessary to distinguish it from other independent multiplayer games. More expressive animations, stronger visual feedback, and greater environmental variety could have improved the overall atmosphere. Its presentation remains functional in concept, but it does little to elevate the experience beyond its basic premise.

The most significant limitation is its multiplayer accessibility. MineFight is designed specifically for two players sharing the same computer, requiring a keyboard and a controller for local competition. There is no advertised single-player campaign or dedicated computer-controlled opponent mode, making the experience unsuitable for anyone hoping to enjoy it independently. Steam Remote Play Together offers a possible way to participate remotely, although this relies on Steam's streaming functionality rather than conventional online matchmaking. These restrictions make the game considerably less convenient than other competitive titles. Even players interested in its mechanics must arrange the appropriate equipment and find someone willing to participate, creating an unnecessary obstacle to casual enjoyment.

Replayability is another area where the experience struggles. While learning arrow physics, experimenting with different characters, and mastering special abilities can provide temporary entertainment, the absence of substantial progression systems or additional gameplay modes limits long-term motivation. Repeated battles may remain enjoyable with a similarly skilled friend, but the game offers little beyond its core competitive encounters. Its free-to-play availability makes these shortcomings easier to overlook, especially for players seeking a quick diversion without financial commitment. However, accessibility in terms of price does not automatically translate into lasting entertainment. The predominantly negative Steam user reception also suggests that the experience has struggled to meet broader player expectations.

Regarding technical accessibility, MineFight has extremely modest Windows system requirements, including 1 GB of RAM and approximately 15 MB of storage space. Despite its lightweight nature, Steam Deck compatibility is classified as Unsupported. The game may be capable of running through SteamOS with additional configuration, but its unusual keyboard-and-controller multiplayer requirements make handheld use particularly inconvenient. Players should not expect a seamless portable experience, and successful operation cannot be guaranteed simply because the hardware exceeds the game's minimum specifications. Those primarily interested in Steam Deck gaming would be better served by titles designed around conventional controller support.

Ultimately, MineFight is an interesting but underdeveloped attempt at combining competitive archery, environmental hazards, and character-based abilities within a Minecraft-inspired setting. Its strongest qualities are its accessible premise, potentially entertaining projectile battles, and occasional tactical surprises created by collectible resources. Unfortunately, its limited gameplay variety, restrictive multiplayer configuration, modest presentation, and lack of meaningful progression substantially weaken its appeal. It may provide a few enjoyable sessions between friends who appreciate simple competitive challenges, but it lacks the refinement and depth required for a stronger recommendation. As a free multiplayer experiment, it is worth trying under the right circumstances, although expectations should remain modest.

A creative but limited archery fighting game with occasional entertaining moments, undermined by restrictive multiplayer requirements, repetitive gameplay, and insufficient depth. 

Rating: 4/10
